lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: establishing the AA criterion

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: Dilate (3, −2) about the origin by factor 4.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A figure is dilated so that a side of length 10 becomes a side of length 20. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 1/2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 10; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 2

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 27° and ∠B = 27°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 27° and ∠E = 27°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a segment not through the centre, under a dilation with scale factor k …
choices: is mapped to a perpendicular segment k times as long
is mapped to a segment of the same length
is mapped to a parallel segment k times as long
is mapped to a segment k² times as long

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: Dilate the point (-7, -2) about the origin with scale factor 5. Give the image.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A figure is dilated so that a side of length 7 becomes a side of length 14. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 65° and ∠B = 26°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 65° and ∠E = 26°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
